articles.title: Galena Cube
articles.summary: Dark charcoal with a fine woven mesh pattern and a soft metallic sheen, like carbon fibre or lead-grey cloth. A dark charcoal-black with a faint silver screen-mesh shimmer in patches; the lines blend to a graphite grey cast with light and dark clouds.
articles.what: Lead sulphide cleaving into perfect cubes, each face a small dull mirror. Up close: A fine diagonal grid of thin lines about 10 px apart, glittering silver-white where they cross, over dark charcoal; it looks like chain-link, a window screen or mesh. The grid fades in and out in large soft patches, so some areas are bright mesh and others nearly plain dark. From a distance: A dark charcoal-black with a faint silver screen-mesh shimmer in patches; the lines blend to a graphite grey cast with light and dark clouds. Measured spec (average): metal 173, roughness 77, coat 49. Shine: satin. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, trim, under stripes.
Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.

Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body, hood, roof: patchy grid reads across broad areas
Accent panels and trim under stripes
Red, orange, white or yellow numbers read; dark ones vanish.
Red or orange bands and stripes: classic accent on dark mesh

pitfalls: Not carbon fibre weave: the old card suggests a weave, but this is a thin lattice of lines with open dark cells
Not solid gunmetal: the grid and patches give visible texture
Avoid: dark numbers, they vanish on the charcoal, next to other greys.
